text: LTV's largest customer places its biggest January order. This lesson turns Harborview Industrial Supply's sales order into a Receivables invoice — and introduces the second open invoice already sitting on Harborview's account.

Sales order SO-48217: four hundred Model CP-220 Control Panels, $145 each, a 5% volume discount bringing it to $55,100, Net 30, shipped from Savannah to Harborview's Charlotte warehouse on January 20th. Shipping it also triggers a freight charge on the new Freight Out account.

AutoInvoice generates INV-HV-30144: $55,100 for the control panels, crediting Product Revenue, plus a separate freight line crediting account 7850, Freight Out. The invoice transfers to Receivables cleanly — nothing about it is wrong.

Harborview's account already carries an older, unrelated open invoice: INV-HV-29890, $6,100, from an earlier shipment, still unpaid. It has nothing to do with SO-48217. Keep both invoice numbers in mind — lesson 13's cash receipt interacts with both of them, and not the way it should.
Up next, lesson thirteen: cash receipts, where Harborview's payment arrives — and gets applied to the wrong invoice.
